Recognize the approach

Editorial design organizes stories, images, and supporting information.

Look for

  • Clear story hierarchy
  • Captions, rules, and controlled measures
  • Type and photography composed together

Your learning goal

Describe the visual decisions before choosing a tool. Then make one small example that uses them deliberately.

Next: Origins

Where it comes from

Editorial design organizes stories, images, and supporting information. Web editorial layouts adapt publishing practices to fluid screens, links, and changing amounts of content.

What to examine

Look at the heading, one control, the image treatment, and the reading order. Explain which decisions establish the style and which make the page usable.

Next: Construction

How to construct it

  1. Use CSS grid for the story structure and set a comfortable paragraph measure.
  2. Create reusable title, body, caption, and pull-quote roles. Keep the mobile reading order logical.

Small practice task

Lay out a project case study with a title, a lead paragraph, two images, and captions. Explain the reading order.

Before you expand it

Test the result at its intended size, on a narrow screen, and with keyboard focus. Preserve editable layers and record the source and license of acquired assets.
